Amounts use integer USD cents. Read-only enquiries and preparation of instructions do not advance the service clock. The customer approves each exact prepared instruction before execution. Repeating the same executed request returns its receipt; a different request is a separate instruction. Deadlines are inclusive. A requested bank update advances to the next scheduled event, whose results become available when it occurs. A final outward payment, disclosure, original deletion or commercial settlement cannot be reversed through this service. No additional funding is available beyond the facilities and receipts recorded for the case. The action references specify the accepted data fields.
# Compromised sender and ambiguous payment acknowledgement
The old sender credential is compromised. `fence_sender` disables only its future sends and keeps receipt access; it does not cancel an already accepted payment. `block_tenant` immediately blocks both old and new sending until the recorded tenant-unlock event. A new clean credential can be activated only after the compromised sender is fenced or the tenant blocked. The tenant has the recorded finite slot capacity: an enabled old send and an enabled old receipt each occupy one slot, and an active new credential occupies one slot. Activation needs a free slot. Choose identity_mode inherited or isolated at activation. Inherited mode allows retry_original; isolated mode has only fresh payments. The clean sender can use the recorded standard and priority clearing arrangements. An active clean sender is needed for new payments. An unfenced old sender remains a live security exposure even if a new sender is active.
The pending old payment amount was already reserved outside available cash. At the acknowledgement event it either posts once to its recorded invoice or is rejected and the reserve returns to cash together with the recorded rejection service credit. That credit is paid only for a rejected original instruction. If receipt access remains enabled, the outcome is published then. `retire_receipt` permanently disables old receipt access after its actual outcome is known. `production_cutover` marks the clean sender ready for continuing business only when old send and receipt access are disabled and the original ambiguous payment has a final acknowledged status. The customer requires this production state at closing. `retry_original` is an end-to-end retry of that same business payment: after POSTED it only returns its original result; after REJECTED it needs the retained original receipt capability and submits precisely the original amount once and changes it to POSTED. Neither credential rotation nor a fresh request automatically shares this identity. `pay` creates a new final payment and does not deduplicate against the historical pending payment. The service accepts a positive new payment even if the invoice is already sufficiently funded; the customer's exact-payment objective still applies. Invoice paid_minor includes actual settled funds only.
The CLEARING record describes two separate processing-window allocations. Before available_minute, each new standard payment consumes its entire principal from the earlier window's remaining allocation early_standard_limit_minor. early_standard_used_minor cumulatively records all such accepted payments against that allocation, across every invoice and every partial payment. Exceeding it is rejected with EARLY_STANDARD_BATCH_CAPACITY. Early payment of an invoice is allowed on the same terms as a currently due invoice. Priority service is not open before available_minute, and later capacity cannot be borrowed in advance. The two windows have separate counters; an unused early allocation is not carried into the later batch, and a payment in either window does not replenish the other. From available_minute onward, each new standard payment consumes its entire principal from standard_limit_minor, measured cumulatively across every invoice. A rejected original-identity retry also consumes its original principal from this same capacity. Retrying an already posted identity consumes no capacity and pays nothing. Capacity cannot be restored by changing credentials, retiring receipts, or paying a different invoice. Priority payments do not consume standard capacity but charge priority_fee_minor for every positive execution, including each partial payment. These fees are additional to supplier principal and are not refundable. A priority payment must still have sufficient cash for both fee and principal. Neither route permits an overdraft.
Unlock `propose_credential_cutover`.
| Action | Data keys | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fence_sender | record_id | Disable that sender's future sends; retain receipt access. |
| block_tenant | record_id | Block the tenant until its recorded unlock event. |
| activate | record_id, identity_mode | Activate a clean replacement credential. |
| retire_receipt | record_id | Retire old receipt capability after final acknowledgement. |
| production_cutover | record_id | Complete clean production cutover. |
| retry_original | record_id, credential_id | Retry the original ambiguous payment identity after its outcome is known. |
| pay | record_id, credential_id, amount_minor, rail | Create a fresh final supplier payment through standard or priority clearing. |

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_credential_cutover`

Prepare a scoped sender fence, finite-capacity credential activation, original-payment retry, capacity-limited standard or paid priority supplier remittance, or production cutover.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
